Updated read-through incorporating SLOOS:

- Policy stance unchanged: FOMC kept the funds rate at 5.25–5.50% and continued QT ($60B Treasuries, $35B agency MBS caps). Statement notes slowing activity, moderating but still-strong job gains, and inflation that has eased but is still elevated; the Committee remains highly attentive to inflation risks and stands ready to adjust policy.
- SLOOS confirmation of tighter credit: Banks reported further tightening in C&I standards and terms for firms of all sizes, wider loan spreads, smaller credit lines, and weaker demand. CRE standards tightened markedly, especially for construction and nonresidential segments, with banks citing collateral valuations and credit quality concerns. Household credit also tightened: stricter criteria and higher minimum FICO thresholds for credit cards and autos, tighter HELOC and RRE categories (particularly non-QM and jumbo), and softer demand.
- Banks’ cited drivers: uncertain economic outlook, reduced risk tolerance, deteriorating credit quality, collateral values (notably CRE), and higher funding costs/liquidity considerations, with earlier deposit outflows still a consideration at some institutions.
- Implication: SLOOS corroborates that tighter bank credit will weigh on growth and hiring in coming quarters, reinforcing the FOMC’s “tighter financial and credit conditions” language. While system resilience tempers tail risks, the credit supply headwind argues for a slightly more negative macro impulse relative to the prior baseline.
